Well i finally did it. Purchased this game when it came out to support the devs and 3 years later i finally finished it. Got to say that i was missing out not playing it when it came out, but i'm glad i waited so i could play the definitive edition.

Characters where super interesting with the new origin characters having their own branching quests and special dialogue. I made a custom character and used a mod to change the party from 4 to 6 so i can enjoy the story of Fane, Ifan, Beast, Red Prince, Sebille but not Lohse ( i kinda hated her since the start of the game on the ship ). Had fun and made them the trusted companions of my custom character and so they followed me into hell and back.

World setting was well done, story interesting but felt short since we already fought the void in the first original sin. Wanted a bit more involvement from Lucian ( not just his minions ) in the story and just at the end.

All and all it was a good rpg game and a cool experience. Worth buying full price if you are a divinity fan like i am. Buy it and seek out your divinity Godwoken.

Outstanding game:
1. Professionally crafted – you have all necessary information, hints, screens and controls. You may tune the toolbar exactly for your needs. It is real pleasure. 
2. Player friendly – it is not forces the player to waste his time. Usually, you may solve battle situation in few ways, you are not obliged to acts exactly as prescribed by the developers, you may solve quests in different way without harm for the storyline. You may save or load the game at any moment you want, there is no need to wait for some check point to save, and it is very, very useful.
Sometimes quests solutions are not evident. But this is subject of interest.
The only thing is not perfect – the automatic camera work. But this is not a problem, just a small comment.

Even now in Early Access, this game is both beautiful, as well as beautifully complex and challenging; compared to the first installment, D:OS 2 takes all the strengths of its predecessor and builds on the weaknesses -- we now have Origin Characters with their own backstories on top of optionally completely custom characters, and not just these Origin Character's individual stories, but also the main, overarching story has received much more attention and love than in the first game.

We can also choose between the races of Human, Lizard, Elves, Dwarfs and, my personal favorite, the Undead; whatever you choose, rest assured that even just your race will have an effect on how you're viewed and treated in the world of D:OS 2.

On top of all of this, Larian has even dared to go completely beyond the conventional by implementing a fully-fledged Game Master Mode -- a feature which to me is extremely interesting, allowing up to five players to enjoy customly created campaigns as a group of up to four adventurers and one Game Master, to create the virtual equivalent of the good old Pen & Paper roleplaying experience.

All in all, this has every chance of becoming not just the best RPG of this year, but also one of the best RPGs period.

And guess what, the game and Larian completely delivered -- one of the best cRPGs ever made!

Arguably one of the best top down RPG's ever made. I won't write an overwhelmingly long review praising it, as there are qutie a few written essays about the game. However, I will say that the praise that the game receives is absolutely of merit. There are so few faults I can find with the game, especially after the free Definitive Edition was introduced.

If the Divinity 3, or any other game that Larian Studio's releases is even half the quality of Divinity 2, then it is still an absolute must buy.

This is an RPG for all gamers, even if you don't like this style of game, you will truly appreciate how engaging and fun it is.

As close to a Dungeons and Dragons experience as you can get in a videogame. Freeroamin' adventurin' murderhoboin' getting into trouble and fighting your way out or playing it cool and talking past the guards, the players have the reins and there are no holds barred.
There are some issues that keep it from reaching high excellence, though. The later parts of the game felt rushed, with obvious cuts to content that leave plot lines hanging. Numerous bugs plague the game, some of which can lose days of progress, while others can make the game trivially easy.

Despite the flaws, I rate this game 7/10. Pick up on sale, with great multiplayer

One of the best games I've ever played!

The Good
+ Amazing world and quest design
+ Combat is difficult but rewarding
+ Lot of cool small details that have real effects in the game world
+ Dialogue is extremely powerful in solving problems

The Bad
- Difficulty spikes if you go exploring too far
- Quite a bit of trial and error with dialogue and ambush situations
- Confusing character specific dialogue mechanic, where some NPCs pretend you've never spoken before and repeat lines if you engage them with another party member.

I really like how most quests have more than one way of completing them. Talking your way through situations is often the best way to go about things, but sometimes you just have to firebomb someone from further away to avoid the unwinnable ambush.
One of the best RPGs ever created, without a doubt. At the start it is very tough and overwhelming, but by the middle of Act 1 the game really starts rolling wild.

What a game! It is as good and satisfying, as it is janky and unfair. Filled to the brim with Larian's dark humor, both in its stories and gameplay. Let's be honest, you don't play this game for the main plot - you play it to see what next blows in your face and challenges you to break it. Compared to the first one, combat is more polished, inventory management and crafting are still painful to work through and available companions are way, way better.

Baldur's Gate 3 but with a better combat system that has much more depth to it. Story is sometimes hard to follow and some puzzles definitely feel like they are from the "you have to check a wiki for this" era of gaming but it was enjoyable nonetheless.

Game also pushes you towards being a murder hobo honestly cause of the XP gain rules (Larian didnt have the xp gain from most encounters thing just yet) but it was fine for me since the combat was so fun. 

If you loved Baldur's Gate 3 and wanted to try something similar with some difference, give it a chance.

Maybe I've gotten old and impatient or simply outgrown the genre, but this is not for me.

I spent 60 hours playing Act 1 a couple times without realizing the whole thing was a tutorial.

Act 2 is twice as big.

There are a total of four acts.

Even if the latter two are only as long as the tutorial, this game will still take me more than two hundred hours, just to finish.

I could tell you about the fantastic quest writing, the amazing characters, the delightful (and frequently funny) voice acting, the creative and deep combat system, the gratifying loot, the adult (both sexual and distressingly dark) world, or even the gorgeous (and performant) art, but most of all, it's simply enormous. It's a joy, and a massive, huge, sprawling one at that.

The game is also (as of December 2019) still being supported with patches, minor add-on content, and interesting stuff like the Dark Eye gamemaster mode campaign, along with user mods of all sorts, some of which have been integrated directly into the game through an optional menu. You really cannot go wrong.

Generally speaking - I am not a fan of turn based games. I prefer real time RPG Combat found in games like Skryim, Fallout, and Witcher 3 (The GOAT).

With that being said, even with it not being my favorite combat method, this game is INCREDIBLE. The story and choice making you can make is very similar to Fallout : New Vegas, where each dialogue matters and has an impact.

In terms of replayability, you can choose across multiple "Origin" characters, who all have deep back stories and the ability for you to influence the future on a very large scheme.

If you like RPGs where you get to make choices, this ranks up in the top 3 for me, which are Fallout : New Vegas, Witcher 3, and Divinity : Original Sin 2.

If you've taken the time to read this entire review, take the plunge and invest the time in this game, because it is insanely good.

An absolute gem. DOS2 has to be one of the most fleshed-out RPGS that I've ever experienced, not since Dragon Age: Origins have I felt such a vast degree of player input. Play as whoever you want from a cast of 6 extremely diverse and well written backstories or make your own character, deciding their look, background and race. Either way you're looking at an incredible amount of choice in terms of the games narrative as well as the combat, which if you're even a slight fan of anything tactical is going to hook you in and become extremely engrossing from beginning to end. I've never really considered myself a huge fan of these old-school top down like games, but DOS2 is such a beast of an experience, with amazing visuals, sound design, an engaging storyline, and systems within systems so deep they'll surprise you even a hundred hours in. This game deserves so much more fanfare and the developers should be commended for this obvious labor of love they crafted so wonderfully. A must play for RPG fans, it will not disappoint.

A beautifully crafted masterpiece that is arguably way too overlooked. From unique character storylines to memorable encounters to endless routes to play, D:OS2 is genuinely one of my favorite games of all time. The pre-recorded voice lines REALLY help you connect with the characters. It may be a bit difficult for newer players, but it's beyond satisfying when you push through a challenging area or boss fight-- it's a genuinely rewarding adventure! I found myself bonding with a lot of the characters who tagged along with me.

The best narrative RPG game I have played so far. Unique turn-based combat where one has to apply logic, deep thinking and even common sense resembles playing chess. The plot itself is not a typical fantasy cliché, let alone a fairy tale for children wherein good always prevails over evil. The storyline in the game flows slowly, but the end seems to be quite rushed. Despite that, you can enjoy gameplay lasting approximately 80 hours. Squad management while playing with bots can be enhanced by a handy system of formations. The bots tend to avoid stepping into harmful surfaces and clouds, resulting in their stuck at various places, but that is just a minor issue. I highly recommend roaming the map in a group of 4 characters, beware of suitable distribution of your teammates for having a team of 4 physical or 4 magic characters may result in future inconveniences. The visual design and voice acting in the game are at the admirable level, the language tends to incline towards Tolkien-ish English, and thus old English perfectly fits for the grim atmosphere of Divinity. The game is divided into several Acts in which you can visit numerous places and maps.
All in all, I can only speak of the pros of this game. If you have 80 hours of free time to spare and fondness for fantasy, this is the masterpiece waiting for thee.
